title: Cauliflower Cheese
subtitle: Cauliflower in a sharp cheese sauce, grilled until golden
excerpt: A British Sunday roast essential: cauliflower florets in a rich cheese sauce made with strong Cheddar and a touch of mustard, finished under a hot grill for a golden, bubbling top.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cauliflower cheese is a fixture of the British Sunday roast, served alongside the meat and roast potatoes as one of the classic accompaniments. The dish developed as part of the British tradition of cooking vegetables in white sauce, a technique that goes back to the Victorian kitchen. The combination of cauliflower with a cheese-enriched béchamel was documented in British cookbooks from the late nineteenth century and became a domestic standard through the twentieth century. The key to a good cauliflower cheese is the sauce: it must be thick enough to coat the florets without running off, sharp enough with mustard to cut through the richness of the cheese, and seasoned assertively. A topping of breadcrumbs mixed with extra cheese adds texture and prevents the sauce from forming a skin under the grill.

recipeTools.notes: A shallow baking dish or roasting tin for the final grilling.
A large saucepan for blanching the cauliflower and making the sauce.

content.text: Par-boil the cauliflower until just tender but still with a slight bite: overcooked florets collapse in the sauce. The sauce must be thick enough to hold its shape in the dish rather than pooling at the bottom. Use a strong, well-aged Cheddar for maximum flavour, and do not let the sauce boil hard once the cheese is added or it may split.

items.preparation: grated; use a strong, mature variety

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan), or heat the grill to high. Cook the cauliflower florets in a large pan of well-salted boiling water for 5 to 6 minutes until just tender. Drain and transfer to a shallow baking dish.

Melt the butter in the same saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 1 to 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste. Gradually add the milk, whisking constantly, until you have a smooth, thick sauce. This takes about 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in 100 g of the Cheddar, the mustard powder, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Taste and adjust. Pour over the cauliflower. Scatter the remaining 50 g of Cheddar over the top.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling, or grill for 5 to 8 minutes if the florets are already hot from blanching. Serve immediately.
